problem: Prior audio-visual navigation agents either cannot ask for help or, like AVLEN, can only send a fixed query ("Help me!") and receive a one-way instruction. This burdens the oracle with planning a full path and gives no way to confirm or clarify.
motivation: Audio goals are often sporadic, noisy, or mixed with distractors, so the agent's goal estimate is uncertain. Human-like bidirectional conversation (the agent proposes a grounded question, the oracle answers yes/no or corrects it) can cut oracle effort and improve navigation. Training this needs a policy for when and how to interact under a budget, plus audio-visual-language data.
key_idea: Model the agent as a budget-aware POSMDP with a learned selector over three options (audio-visual navigation, direct instruction query, question-answer). A differential reward penalizes only wrong questions, so the agent learns to forecast trajectories that turn into correct grounded questions.
insight: The learned RL selector beats heuristic triggers (Random, Uniform, Model Uncertainty), e.g. unheard SR 42.0 vs 33.3 for Model Uncertainty. The differential reward is important: delta_ques=0 gives unheard SR 42.0, against 36.5 at 0.5 and 32.1 at 1.0. The selector learns an implicit uncertainty split: goal policy at high confidence, question policy at moderate confidence, direct query at low confidence. The 3-branch design beats the best 2-branch variant (question branch with oracle instructions) by 5.3 SR.
method: Budget-aware POSMDP: a selector policy pi_s picks among options pi_g (single-step audio-visual navigation), pi_l (instruction-guided, nu steps) and pi_ques (question-answer, nu steps). All are trained end-to-end with DD-PPO, and the number of oracle instructions is budgeted.

Differential reward design: pi_g uses the SoundSpaces reward (+1 approach, +10 stop, -0.01 per step). Direct instructions carry a penalty that grows with query count k (linear below budget K, exponential toward -0.6 above it) plus a frequency penalty. Questions are penalized only when the oracle answers 'no' (delta_ques=0 for correct ones), with K+K'=3.

TrajectoryNet: a transformer encoder-decoder takes ego occupancy maps from 4 views (90° apart) and the audio-goal vector, and autoregressively forecasts 4 navigation actions. Occupancy-map input gives the best forecasting accuracy (58.1% at 4 steps, vs 50.3% for RGB-D and 38.7% for RGB).

QuestionNet: a transformer over 12 panoramic views (ResNet-152 RGB features plus occupancy-map CNN features) fused with the forecasted end view g_view and displacement g_sub. It decodes the question word by word (CLIP or GloVe embeddings). It also generates oracle-side instructions when the question is wrong.

FollowerNet: on the oracle side, it decodes the question into one of 12 direction sectors. The oracle answers 'yes' if this lies within 30° of its estimated goal direction, otherwise 'no' plus a short guiding instruction.

AVN-Instruct dataset: QuestionNet and FollowerNet are pre-trained on Landmark-RxR (150k sub-trajectories). Only ~3k trajectories map onto the SoundSpaces grid by direct approximation, so 38.5k more are self-supervised, giving 41.5k audio-goal / action-sequence / sub-instruction triplets.
New metrics SNI and SNO: success rate divided by the average number of language interactions (SNI), or by the number of direct oracle instructions including wrong questions (SNO).

setting.backbone: Transformer encoder-decoder audio-visual policy (SAVi-style) + TrajectoryNet, QuestionNet, FollowerNet transformers + selector policy, trained with DD-PPO
setting.training_data: SoundSpaces semantic audio-goal episodes (500k train episodes, 85 scans); Landmark-RxR 150k sub-instructions for pre-training; synthesized AVN-Instruct 41.5k triplets
setting.observation: Egocentric RGB-D (panoramic 12 views for question generation) + binaural audio; depth turned into ego occupancy maps
setting.action_space: Discrete low-level: MOVE_FORWARD 1 m / TURN_LEFT / TURN_RIGHT 90° / STOP, plus language interaction options (question, query)
setting.privileged: An oracle (simulated human) with GT geodesic action information answers questions and gives instructions, with a limited budget; the GT Actions variant uses GT action feedback

numbers_note: The paper does not use the canonical benchmark list; the SoundSpaces semantic audio-goal task is tagged 'other:'. Success is printed as 'Success' and mapped to SR. The GT Actions heard-sound row is also reported (SR 54.8, SPL 41.4) but omitted.
results: On unheard sounds CAVEN with language feedback reaches SR 42.0 / SPL 30.0, against 26.2 / 17.6 for AVLEN (language) and 36.7 / 24.1 for AVLEN (GT actions). On heard sounds it reaches SR 48.4 versus 36.1 for AVLEN. It stays ahead of AVLEN with a noisy oracle, gains about 12 SNO over AVLEN, and beats AVLEN under distractor sounds (SR 21.3 vs 14.0).
limitations: Interaction is English-only, and QuestionNet/FollowerNet are pre-trained on Landmark-RxR, which is sparser than SoundSpaces and may not cover all object categories, risking underfitting.
The agent may have to wait for oracle feedback; the oracle is simulated, and evaluation is in simulation only.
The agent asks correct questions only about 40% of the time, so a large share of interactions still burns the instruction budget.
